source_review.notes: Reviewed Bayer-McCreight's original B-tree paper, Lomet's primary concurrency/deletion paper, Morin's author-maintained formal treatment, CMU's tree-index notes, current official PostgreSQL documentation and nbtree maintainer notes, and current official SQLite module and source documentation. All eight final destinations returned HTTP 200. The chapter distinguishes classic B-tree proofs from B+ and product-specific implementations.

evidence: Checked minimum degree t>=2, node key count m, height h in edges, population n, key sequences, child gaps, and root/nonroot exceptions.
Checked strict-order notation is consistently qualified by an explicit composite duplicate policy.
Checked node-page visits, physical I/O, CPU comparison cost, encoded bytes, latch state, page generation, and LSN are separate quantities.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The chapter explicitly avoids the ambiguous literature term order and states exact minimum-degree bounds.

evidence: Recomputed t=2 insertion trace: final root 10,20; leaves 5,6,7 | 12,17 | 30; height one; sorted conservation of eight keys.
Recomputed Example 1 at t=50,h=3: minimum 2*50^3-1=249999 and maximum 100^4-1=99999999.
Recomputed byte-capacity example: 96 fixed + m*(16+40) + (m+1)*8 = 104+64m, so a 4096-byte page bounds m at floor(3992/64)=62.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Byte capacity is deliberately conservative and excludes any unstated alignment or metadata; implementations must recompute from exact encoding.

evidence: Re-derived minimum keys as 1 + 2(t-1) sum from i=0 to h-1 of t^i = 2t^h-1 for h>=1.
Re-derived maximum keys in a full 2t-ary tree as (2t)^(h+1)-1 and height upper bound floor(log base t of (n+1)/2).
Verified split, rotation, merge, and root growth/contraction conserve ordered membership, separator ranges, legal occupancy, and equal leaf depth under their stated preconditions.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Count-based theorems are not claimed for unconstrained variable-length byte occupancy.

evidence: Reviewed empty/singleton root, exact minimum/maximum nodes, root split, cascading split, all internal/leaf deletion cases, both rotations, merge edges, and root contraction.
Reviewed duplicates, maximum encoded keys/records, overflow, prefix boundaries, corrupt counts/ranges/child IDs, arithmetic overflow, cycles, shared children, and hostile page bytes.
Reviewed latch/restart races, deadlock, stale generation, late I/O/WAL, split/merge crash points, allocator leaks/double ownership, torn writes, mixed versions, and live-verifier snapshots.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: The executable model covers unique integer insertion only; deletion, bytes, I/O, concurrency, recovery, and faults remain explicitly outside its evidence.

evidence: The finite validator checks key count, strict local order, ancestor range, child count, leaf child absence, and equal leaf depths recursively.
The insertion algorithm splits every full root or child before descent and promotes the exact median, so the recursive target is nonfull.
Exact outputs check two membership paths, final root/leaves, height, in-order conservation, and aggregate validity.
invariant_checking.notes: The model's root minimum permits the empty representation although the exercised trace is nonempty.

evidence: Reviewed the population/height induction from root exceptions, minimum branching, geometric sum, and logarithmic inversion.
Reviewed insertion and all top-down deletion transformations including separator-mediated rotations, child-pointer transfer, exact merge capacity, and root contraction.
Reviewed refinement obligations for variable bytes, parser validation, structural publication, WAL/root/allocation recovery, latching, reclamation, and independent reachability audit.
proof_review.notes: Storage arguments are design proof obligations, not a mechanized refinement or verified production implementation.

evidence: Height, abstract transformations, and storage realization are separate labeled proof structures.
Classic B-tree record promotion is distinguished from B+ leaf-only copying and linked-leaf semantics reserved for DSE-073.
Source examples, finite model execution, test prescriptions, and production measurements are not represented as mathematical or universal proof.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Every concurrency, durability, corruption, and performance conclusion is scoped to evidence that would actually test that layer.

evidence: The standard-library Python model passed exact twelve-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under the repository verifier.
It reproduced two preemptive splits, root 10,20, three same-depth leaves, successful 17 and unsuccessful 15 paths, exact in-order contents, and valid=True.
All eight external destinations returned HTTP 200 and repository-local structure and link validation passed.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No deletion implementation, byte codec, real page I/O, buffer pool, concurrent schedule, WAL, crash recovery, fuzz campaign, performance benchmark, migration, or repair was executed.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter derives B-tree height and transformations from precise minimum-degree invariants, distinguishes classic record placement from B+, and maps abstract correctness to explicit page, concurrency, durability, and operational obligations.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed worst-case byte fan-out, duplicate identity, split/merge feasibility, page parsing, latch/version protocols, delayed reclamation, structural WAL and allocator recovery, snapshot verification, migration/rollback, fuzz/crash testing, telemetry, and performance gates.

pedagogical_review.notes: The one-page review provides the invariant set and theorem; the exact insertion model makes preemptive splitting concrete; ten examples cover proof, insertion, every deletion mechanism, bytes, concurrency, crash, and evidence; five exercises include complete derivations and an engineering audit.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/maintainer-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, Bayer, McCreight, Lomet, Morin, CMU, PostgreSQL, SQLite, database, storage-engine, concurrency, formal-methods, security, reliability, performance, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and model prove neither deletion code, variable-byte occupancy, a page format/parser, buffer pool, concurrent tree, safe reclamation, WAL/recovery, allocator correctness, corruption tolerance, migration, production performance, certification, nor deployment fitness.
